title: Quantifying evaluation leakage in multi-species gene-disease link prediction: a graded audit and de-leaked benchmark
description:
Code, de-leaked evaluation splits, and benchmark results accompanying the manuscript "Quantifying evaluation leakage in multi-species gene-disease link prediction: a graded audit and a de-leaked benchmark."

Resource. A graded leakage audit of gene-disease link prediction on a multi-species, Monarch-derived knowledge graph (452,012 nodes; 5,860,539 directed edges; 28 relation types across 8 node categories). The graph is approximately 98.5% Monarch Initiative content augmented with seven curated non-Monarch sources (DGIdb, GWAS Catalog, DrugCentral, Orphadata, Gene2Phenotype, CIViC, DIDA); it is a Monarch-derived knowledge graph, not an equal integration of many independent databases.

Benchmark. Four knowledge-graph-embedding models spanning two families (translational: TransE, RotatE; bilinear: DistMult, ComplEx) and five topological baselines (Random, Common-Neighbors, Adamic-Adar, Jaccard, Preferential-Attachment) are evaluated under one shared ranking harness on 4,228 held-out human gene-disease test edges, across four leakage regimes: R0 (standard random split), R1 (redundancy; direct held-pair edges removed), R2 (degree-preserving null; degree sequence exactly preserved), and R3 (orthology-blocked; cross-species ORTHOLOGOUS_TO bridges removed). Three training seeds (42, 1, 7).

Main finding. Evaluation leakage is method-class-dependent. Node-degree structure (R2) is the one universal leak (topological baselines drop ~43-49% MRR, KGE models ~21-37%, separating by family); train/test redundancy (R1) leaks only into multi-hop KGE (~6-13%) and is invisible to overlap heuristics; cross-species orthology (R3) is a designed negative control that comes back null. A filtered full-ranking robustness check (each true disease ranked against the entire ~14.3k-disease pool rather than 50 sampled negatives) reproduces and strengthens the degree effect, with KGE models collapsing 70-82% under full ranking.

Contents. De-leaked splits and split manifest (data/processed/splits/); per-regime baseline and KGE result JSONs including the full-ranking robustness run (data/processed/results/); table and figure generators (scripts/make_tables.py, scripts/make_figures.py) that read only the frozen result JSONs (no hand-entered numbers); and a one-command regeneration script (run_all.sh). All runs use fixed seeds; paths are repo-relative with no secrets or hard-coded machine paths.
